summary: tailwind-forms-kit executes remote attacker code on import via blockchain-resolved C2
details: The package masquerades as a copy of @tailwindcss/forms but prepends an obfuscated IIFE to src/index.js that runs the moment the module is required. The loader is reconstructed from a ~190-element base64 string array, atob-decoded and eval'd. The decoded loader queries public Ethereum RPC/Blockscout endpoints (eth.blockscout.com/api) for transactions from sender 0xa322E5f3D311D3080e6f0121063e9aDC2490Ef1a and extracts a C2 IP address from the `to` field of a transaction (EtherHiding technique), then fetches an XOR-encoded second-stage payload from http://<resolved-ip>:443/0x/cls and /0x/ls, decrypts it, and eval's it. The loader additionally spawns a detached, stdio-ignored, windowsHide node subprocess running the attacker-supplied code via `node -e`, which outlives the parent process. The package name resembling @tailwindcss/forms is the lure; the native tailwindcss/forms content is cover for the install-time fetch-and-eval chain.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
